study: Yang, Porter, Massey, Merlino & Desimone 2020, middle-school science PD (Cog-sci curriculum vs Content vs BAU), JRST
eval_evidence: Study authored/conducted by the program developers (National R&D Center on Cognition and Science Instruction, IES grant R305C080009); no independent third-party evaluator.
developer_evidence: The research/developer team itself delivered the PD: 'For both arms, we provided a 2.5-day (18-hr) summer PD session and four 2-hr PLC sessions ... for 2 years' (p.9).
cascade_evidence: The project team delivered the summer institutes and PLC meetings directly to the participating teachers; no train-the-trainer/lead-teacher intermediary.
counterfactual_evidence: Three-arm RCT with a 'business-as-usual control condition'; control schools taught the standard (unmodified Holt) curriculum with no alternative PD (pp.2, 4).
coaching_evidence: PD was a 2.5-day summer institute plus ~monthly professional learning community (PLC) meetings during each unit; no in-class coaching/observation cycles in teachers' own classrooms.
student_dose_evidence: Cog-sci arm modifies what is taught in the regular science class (cognitive-science-principle-infused Holt units); Content arm changes teacher knowledge only — no added tutoring, extra minutes, or student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Program is a defined two-year (grade 7-8) sequence; end-of-treatment state-science-test outcome is at the end of grade 8 for each cohort, no separate first-vs-mature implementation-year axis (Cohort 2 included many returning teachers).
